question: What is the correct recipe for the new moon sacrifice?
summary: Numbers 28:11-15 prescribes the new moon offering as two young bulls, one ram, seven male lambs, and a goat for sin offering. Ezekiel 46:6 prescribes one bull, one ram, and six lambs. Two different sacrificial recipes for the same monthly festival.

reconcile.connective: Defenders concede the numbers differ but read Ezekiel's temple vision as a distinct, future economy whose offerings were never meant to match the Mosaic recipe.

discrepancy.connective: Julius Wellhausen pressed exactly these Ezekiel-vs-Pentateuch sacrificial divergences as evidence that the two cannot be a single law, arguing the Priestly festival legislation post-dates Ezekiel rather than being presupposed by him.

skeptic.name: Julius Wellhausen
skeptic.work: Prolegomena to the History of Israel
skeptic.attribution: Julius Wellhausen (d. 1918), Prolegomena to the History of Israel (Eng. trans. 1885; German 1878)

pd_work.resource: John Gill, Exposition of the Entire Bible (1746-63), on Ezekiel 46:5
pd_work.author: John Gill
pd_work.note: Gill treats this passage directly, granting the offerings differ from Numbers 28 and reconciling the difference as a deliberate feature of a distinct future economy (citing Kimchi's 'new thing to be done in future time').

link.note: No allowlisted page treats this specific Ezekiel-vs-Numbers offering-recipe discrepancy; defendinginerrancy's Ezekiel 40-48 page addresses only the Ezekiel-vs-NT abolition-of-sacrifice question, so it is omitted rather than overstated.

excerpts.attribution: John Gill, Exposition of the Entire Bible (1746-63)
excerpts.excerpt_text: This is also different from the law of Moses, which required two young bullocks and a ram, and seven lambs, Num 28:11, whereas here only one bullock: and six lambs, and a ram; they shall be without blemish; and here Kimchi acknowledges again that this is a new thing to be done in future time.
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Names the exact recipe difference (2 bulls/1 ram/7 lambs vs 1 bull/1 ram/6 lambs) and harmonizes it as a deliberate 'new thing... in future time' rather than the same law — the strongest single on-tension reconcile.
excerpts.source_note_text:
And in the day of the new moon it shall be a young bullock without blemish,.... This is also different from the law of Moses, which required two young bullocks and a ram, and seven lambs, Num 28:11, whereas here only one bullock:
and six lambs, and a ram; they shall be without blemish; and here Kimchi acknowledges again that this is a new thing to be done in future time. Some have observed, that the seven lambs under the law showed that perfection might be hoped for and expected; but, there being but six now, that this is not yet attained, nor will be till the saints get to heaven; though perfection is come by the priesthood of Christ, whose sacrifice is a perfect and complete one, and by which his people are perfected, and they are complete in him, yet they have no perfection in themselves.
